name: Saarland
summary: The German black, red and gold tricolour with the state arms in the centre, quartering the arms of Nassau-Saarbrücken, Trier, Lorraine and Palatinate-Zweibrücken.
origin: After the Second World War, Saarland was a French protectorate with its own flag, a white Nordic cross on blue and red. After a 1955 referendum it joined West Germany on 1 January 1957, adopting its current flag.

symbols.name: Quartered arms
symbols.description: A silver lion on blue; a red cross on white; three white eagles on a red band on gold; a golden lion on black.

history.label: Saar Protectorate
history.note: White cross on blue and red.

facts: Saarland was separated from Germany twice in the 20th century.
It is the smallest German state that is not a city-state.
clues: The German tricolour with a quartered shield of lions, a cross and eagles.
Its region was a French protectorate until 1956.
